newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU seen agreeing modified cotton dumping plan.
newsitem.headline: EU seen agreeing modified cotton dumping plan.

text.p: The European Union is likely to agree on Friday a modified plan for definitive anti-dumping duties on cotton imports from China, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Turkey and Pakistan, a European Commission spokesman said on Thursday.

He said after a second meeting of EU ambassadors on Thursday that there was "quite a strong likelihood" that national capitals would now agree to the Commission's modified proposal for duties on unbleached cotton imports from the countries named.
Diplomats said earlier on Thursday that nine of the EU's 15 countries had rejected the proposal, making it likely the plan would lapse come the May 20 expiry date for provisional duties.
But a Commission offer to review the duties after one year appeared to have swung three countries -- Austria, Germany and Luxembourg -- behind the six who originally backed the plan.

"The Commission saw how finely balanced the thing was," the spokesman said in reference both to EU countries' positions and to the conflicting positions on duties of EU cotton producers and cotton finishers.
"The best thing for the Commission to do was to modify the proposal so that a full review can take place within the shortest possible time -- That is to say one year," he added.
